meta.exam_title: Visions of the future – Written Exam No. 4

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling weist darauf hin, wie der World State mittels klassischer Konditionierung Verhalten kontrolliert, etwa:
bullets: explains that infants are trained to associate books and flowers with pain through electric shocks and loud noise
points out that this creates an instinctive, lifelong aversion to knowledge and nature
notes that the conditioning is deliberately repeated to make it irreversible
explains that the method relies on linking a neutral stimulus with an unpleasant one to shape behaviour
points out that the children cannot resist or question the process due to their age and helplessness

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling weist darauf hin, wie Kastensystem und genetische Vorbestimmung Konformität sichern, etwa:
bullets: explains that citizens are mass-produced in identical groups rather than born individually
points out that caste membership is assigned before birth and marked visibly through uniform clothing
notes that this removes individual identity and predetermines each citizen's role
explains that uniformity of appearance and behaviour prevents citizens from questioning their place
points out that the institutional setting frames this as a normal, administrative process

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling weist darauf hin, wie ökonomisches Verhalten gezielt gesteuert wird, etwa:
bullets: explains that citizens are conditioned to dislike nature but love activities requiring manufactured equipment
points out that this ensures continuous consumption of goods and transport
notes that consumer behaviour is engineered rather than left to individual choice
explains that this links psychological conditioning directly to the World State's economic stability

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie Setting/Atmosphäre (inkl. Farbsymbolik), Figurenverhalten und Sprache zusammenwirken, um die wachsende Spannung in der Szene zu erzeugen, z. B.:
bullets: combines the idyllic opening imagery with the abrupt tonal shift after the explosion (l. 22–36)
links the shift from gentle, childlike diction to violent, clinical language to the babies' conditioning
notes how the Director's calm authority contrasts with the children's escalating distress
identifies the closing religious allusion ("What man has joined...", l. 57) as underscoring the irreversibility of the conditioning

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert, wie Setting und Atmosphäre – auch mittels Farbsymbolik – zur Spannungssteigerung beitragen, z. B.:
bullets: highlights the initial bright, sunny setting ("very bright and sunny", l. 2) as deceptively idyllic
points out the multi-ethnic colour imagery of the rose petals ("pink and Aryan... luminously Chinese... pale as death", l. 6–8) as foreshadowing artificial uniformity
notes the sun "coming out of a momentary eclipse" (l. 23) intensifying the roses' colour just before the shock
identifies the shift from warm, natural imagery to the mechanical "switchboard" (l. 34) marking the tonal turn
points out the description of the room as "large" and "bare" (l. 2) suggesting a sterile space beneath the initial warmth
notes how light/colour imagery disappears once the shocks begin, replaced by sound (siren, bells)

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert, wie das Verhalten der Figuren die Spannung steigert, z. B.:
bullets: points out the nurses' immediate, silent obedience ("stiffened to attention", l. 9) establishing control
notes the Director's curt commands ("he said curtly", l. 10) contrasted with his later triumphant tone (l. 53)
highlights the babies' initial excitement ("little squeals... gurgles and twitterings of pleasure", l. 26–27)
points out the abrupt change to "screamed", "faces... distorted with terror" (l. 38)
identifies the Director's detached explanatory stance ("bawled... in explanation", l. 45) as unsettling
notes the student's silent admiration (l. 65) as an unsettling normalisation of the scene

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert, wie sprachliche Mittel zur Spannungssteigerung eingesetzt werden, z. B.:
bullets: points out the short, imperative sentences ("Set out the books.", l. 10) conveying authority
highlights the accumulation of violent, sensory verbs ("shrieked", "maddeningly sounded", l. 36)
notes the juxtaposition of childlike diminutives ("cock-a-doodle-doo", l. 52) with clinical vocabulary ("electrify", l. 45)
points out the comparison "as if to the tug of unseen wires" (l. 44) dehumanising the infants
identifies the ironic biblical allusion in "What man has joined, nature is powerless to put asunder" (l. 57)
notes the escalating adverbs ("Shriller and ever shriller", l. 36) mirroring rising tension

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erörtert das Zitat vor dem Hintergrund der Begriffsgeschichte von Utopie und Dystopie, z. B.:
bullets: explains Thomas More's coinage of "utopia" as a pun on the Greek "no place"/"good place"
points out that Wilde's paradox reframes utopia as a necessary, ever-receding goal
discusses how the excerpt presents a realised "utopia" that functions as a dystopia
relates the World State's engineered conformity to the loss of the aspirational quality Wilde describes
evaluates whether Huxley's dystopia confirms or challenges Wilde's optimistic view
discusses the tension between Wilde's optimism and the static, controlled society in the extract

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt Bezüge zu im Unterricht behandelten dystopischen Werken her, um die These zu stützen oder zu hinterfragen, z. B.:
bullets: compares the World State's conditioning to control mechanisms in The Hunger Games
compares the suppression of independent thought to censorship in Fahrenheit 451
discusses similarities between Huxley's engineered conformity and class-based control in the works studied
evaluates whether these works also present dystopia as a corrupted realisation of a utopian ideal
points out differences in how each work stages resistance (or its absence)
draws a conclusion about recurring features of literary dystopias across the works studied

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nimmt begründet und differenziert Stellung zu Wildes These, z. B.:
bullets: takes a clear position on whether striving for an unattainable ideal is valuable or futile
supports the position with reasons drawn from the texts discussed and/or examples
considers a counter-argument before refuting or qualifying it
discusses risks of pursuing "utopian" projects, referencing Huxley's dystopian outcome
reflects on the relevance of Wilde's idea for contemporary society
reaches a well-founded, coherent conclusion

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt die Bedeutung dystopischer Literatur für die heutige Gesellschaft dar, z. B.:
bullets: explains that dystopian fiction makes abstract societal risks tangible and emotionally accessible
points out parallels between fictional control mechanisms and real contemporary developments
discusses why readers continue to engage with dystopian narratives despite their bleakness
relates the significance of the genre to its capacity for social critique
draws on the framing device (waking from a nightmare) to underline its unsettling relevance
evaluates why dystopian fiction remains significant across different historical periods

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert die Rolle, die dystopischer Literatur in der Gesellschaft zukommt, z. B.:
bullets: explains the genre's function as a warning system against harmful societal developments
points out its role in encouraging critical reflection on power structures
discusses how dystopian fiction offers a safe, fictional space to confront uncomfortable possibilities
relates this role to the mechanisms of control shown in the Huxley excerpt
considers the role of dystopian fiction in shaping public discourse
evaluates limitations of this role (e.g. desensitisation or fatalism)

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling begründet die Wichtigkeit dystopischer Literatur für die moderne Gesellschaft, z. B.:
bullets: argues why continued engagement with dystopian narratives matters given current challenges
points out how the genre can motivate readers towards civic or political engagement
discusses the importance of the genre in a media-saturated, information-driven society
draws a connection to the loss of individuality depicted in the extract
considers counter-arguments (e.g. "merely entertainment") before refuting them
reaches a well-founded conclusion on the genre's continued importance

criteria.intro: Wortschatz — Der Prüfling beachtet die Normen der sprachlichen Korrektheit im Sinne einer gelingenden Kommunikation.
Grammatik
Orthografie
Der Prüfling gibt den im Ausgangstext beschriebenen Mechanismus der Konditionierung wieder, etwa:
bullets: explains classical conditioning (Pavlov) as the theoretical basis of reward-based behaviour change
notes that the text uses Pavlov's dog experiment (bell and food) as the classic illustrating example
explains operant conditioning (Skinner) as a further development, where reinforcement follows the behaviour
points out that a reward given often enough eventually maintains the behaviour without further rewards
gives the sweets-for-sitting-still example as an illustration of the mechanism
explains that rewards function as a substitute stimulus shaping long-term behaviour
points out that the mechanism relies on a learned, not natural, association
relates the mechanism to the hope that reward-givers have for lasting behavioural change

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt die im Ausgangstext beschriebene langfristige Wirksamkeit von Belohnungen dar, etwa:
bullets: points out that studies show reward-based motivation often decreases once rewards are withdrawn
gives the 1976 study on children and maths games as evidence
gives the example of reward-based smoking cessation showing lower long-term success than a control group
mentions similarly poor long-term results for reward-based weight-loss/communication programmes
explains that rewards may work short-term but underperform no intervention at all long-term
draws the conclusion that reward programmes generally fail to achieve durable change
relates these findings to the discrepancy between intended and actual long-term effect
notes that the overall pattern across the studies mentioned is one of reduced effectiveness

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert im Ausgangstext genannte mögliche Fehlvorstellungen, etwa:
bullets: points out the misconception that visible short-term compliance proves rewards are working
explains that rewards can distract givers from investigating the actual reasons behind a behaviour
points out the misconception that rewarded people are necessarily more competent, when they may be concealing problems
explains that reward systems can reduce willingness to admit mistakes or ask for help
notes the risk that reward programmes discourage independent problem-solving
points out that engaged behaviour under a reward scheme is not evidence of genuine motivation
notes that this misconception can prevent addressing underlying difficulties (e.g. task difficulty)

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling richtet seinen Text konsequent und explizit auf die Intention und den Adressatenkreis im Sinne der Aufgabenstellung aus, berücksichtigt den situativen Kontext, beachtet die Textsortenmerkmale des geforderten Zieltextformats, erstellt einen sachgerecht strukturierten Text und gestaltet seinen Text hinreichend ausführlich, aber ohne unnötige Wiederholungen und Umständlichkeiten.

Der Prüfling löst sich vom Wortlaut des Ausgangstextes und formuliert eigenständig, ggf. unter Verwendung von Kompensationsstrategien, verwendet funktional einen sachlich wie stilistisch angemessenen und differenzierten allgemeinen, thematischen und Funktionswortschatz und verwendet einen variablen und dem jeweiligen Zieltextformat angemessenen Satzbau.
Der Prüfling beachtet die Normen der sprachlichen Korrektheit im Sinne einer gelingenden Kommunikation (Wortschatz, Grammatik, Orthografie).
